narrative: A Syrian man left for Turkey as the violence escalated, and from Turkey, with a friend and the friend's younger brother, reached Greece. They decided to head for Serbia through Macedonia, walking along the railway tracks in freezing temperatures, fending off gangs that tried to rob them. After three days walking toward Serbia, the police arrested them near the Serbian border and sent them back to Greece. Exhausted, they rested in Greece for two days and treated their injuries, then tried again; this time they crossed into Serbia after four days on foot. From Serbia they tried to cross into Hungary, where the border was equipped with thermal cameras to detect anyone passing. They offered some police money to let them through, but the officers took the money and still would not let them pass. After repeated attempts they finally crossed into Hungary, but on learning that some locals reported refugees to the police, they joined another group and headed for Germany. He applied for asylum in Germany, but the authorities rejected his request because he already had an asylum application in Hungary, under the Dublin rules; he explained that he had been forced, but the German authorities still refused.
